name: Rembrandt
hook: The Dutch master of light: one night watch, one anatomy lesson, and hundreds of etchings.

facts.label: The Night Watch
facts.statement: The Night Watch (1642), officially the company of Captain Frans Banning Cocq, hangs in Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum.

facts.label: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
facts.statement: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp shows a dissection in Amsterdam, with Dr. Tulp demonstrating the procedure.

facts.label: Aristotle Contemplating the Bust of Homer
facts.statement: Aristotle Contemplating the Bust of Homer was one of the few Rembrandt paintings sent abroad during his lifetime.

facts.label: his etchings
facts.statement: Rembrandt made about 300 etchings, turning an acid-and-metal-plate process into an art form; in his day his print reputation outshone his painting.

facts.label: Samson
facts.statement: Rembrandt painted biblical scenes including Samson Threatening His Father-in-Law and The Blinding of Samson.

facts.label: Saskia
facts.statement: Saskia, Rembrandt's wife and portrait subject, died three years after the couple moved into his Amsterdam house.

facts.label: the Rembrandt tulip
facts.statement: A streaked variety of tulip is named for Rembrandt; the unusual markings were originally caused by a virus.
